decisions.reason: Confirmed a false smallness conclusion, not a defect in the Euler formula: already for one vertex without arrows, the vector spaces on underlying sets K x {alpha}, for arbitrary ordinals alpha, give a proper class of distinct objects. The finite-field matrix-orbit construction proves smallness only of the full skeleton. Corrected the Statement and step 6.1 to distinguish the essentially small category from its small finitary abelian skeleton, and explained transport of Yoneda classes to the skeleton.

reviews.reason: Reviewed the representation definition, actual finitary interface, endpoint-fixed Yoneda equivalence, short-five-lemma interface, owning contract and page. Vertexwise kernels/cokernels establish abelianness; path-length reduction and the unique first arrow establish exactness and injectivity of the length-one projective resolution. Off-diagonal block matrices classify Yoneda extensions as coker(partial), and rank-nullity gives the stated Euler orientation. The explicit finite-field orbit representatives form a set of objects with a set of morphisms; transporting kernels, cokernels and extension middle terms gives a small finitary skeleton without arbitrary choice. Corrected only the smallness conclusion and its final proof inference. This is a repair-time review, not independent review of my own repair.
